# Execution clarifications and retained failures

Before trials, source inspection found C1's `nodeFloor` input is a closed literal `20.3.0`.
The declaration therefore uses that required literal while the actual executable is pinned Node
24.15.0, satisfying NormProof's >=24 requirement. No Node 20 compatibility claim is made.
The preregistered runtime/artifact/commands are unchanged. No model request or experimental trial
ran before preregistration commit f34cffb.

Initial source snapshot extraction failed on a tracked absolute symlink; a second attempt tried
to overwrite the already-read-only snapshot. Both setup failures are retained under logs. Exact
archives were retained and all materialized regular file bytes checked against their archive.
Symlinks are preserved as links and are never followed for experiment input or mutation.

Setup01 (five C01 trajectories, not scored) observed Stop unknown/empty_output even when the
workspace is proven by both MCP and CLI. Live source and the N3-5 historical commit confirm
`--emit-result` is implemented for gate write only. Gate stop silently ignores it and emits
nothing for allow. This is a measured compatibility gap, not a reason to modify either product
or substitute another Stop command. Keep the exact registered Stop treatment and report unknown.
The N3 execution document's old commit IDs were rewritten; current main has the same relevant
behavior. N2/N3/C2 source is present but separate completion of those projects does not establish
end-to-end compatibility. No experimental inference that all prerequisites integrate is made.

Before scored runs, instrumentation was completed: child startup logging counts real invocations;
native prepared patch execution is observed without replacing its permission or execution owner;
the scripted patch uses native `input` rather than an invalid `patch` argument. Frozen inputs and
oracle are unchanged. Setup01 logs remain. The actual Node runtime remains 24.15.0 throughout.

Smoke01 real provider: four HTTP 200 requests reached native reads and a successful write;
the fifth request timed out at the preregistered 120 s request deadline. The trial is retained as
a development smoke, not replaced or scored in the fixed schedule. It is not a product failure.
No uncertain write is retried; the final filesystem and all observed events are preserved.

Calibration initial passes (80 runs, prefix calibration) found C08 never reached its intended
PreToolUse seam: native apply_patch requires an explicit group selection even under allow-all.
This is a harness omission. The full initial passes remain as observed and are not merged into
the calibrated estimand. The harness now supplies the experiment-authorized one-time selection
using the native prompt's exact revision, and creates a real isolated session via SessionManager.
The same frozen 80 cases are rerun as calibration-fixed; both cohorts and their counts are reported.
No task/oracle/rule/seed or product source changed. Real held-out trials have not begun.

While the first live pass runs, the runner startup now checks its durable provider-stop record
before beginning a second pass. This corrects the shell sequence so the preregistered stop applies
across both passes; it changes no active trial. A stopped pass is never automatically resumed.

Final formal live sequence: T03/post-action, T03/combined, T02/CI-only each failed its first
provider request at the 120 s deadline. The pass wrote `results/stop-live-p1.json`; pass two
exited before configuration or network calls. Formal sample is 3/60 attempted, with 57 unrun;
two arms have n=0/unavailable. This does not satisfy the intended live five-arm comparison.

Aggregation explicitly distinguishes compliant residual source from completion of a scripted
write task. A denied draft leaves compliant baseline files but did not perform its fixed task;
false-completion and recovery tables require the requested exact file bytes as well as compliance.
The raw `final.complete` field is the frozen source oracle's result when no functional task was
passed, so on scripted rows it represents compliance only; report.py applies the frozen task
requirement separately. No oracle or raw result was rewritten.

Installed dependency bytes were inventoried after execution in `dependency-manifests.json`.
Package/lockfile identities were registered before execution, but a whole installed dependency
tree digest was not. Same-process fixed replays observed stable results; future reproduction
checks every installed byte and refuses drift. This is a provenance limitation, not a claim
that npm install always produces identical bytes.

Final report verification initially found CRLF CSV lines reported as trailing whitespace by
`git diff --check`. The first validation receipt incorrectly marked that gate passed before its
result was inspected. This was a reporting error, corrected explicitly: CSV serialization now
uses LF; the original gate failure is retained and the corrected gate reruns below. No measured
sample, judgement, preregistration or oracle changed. Development scripted and live smokes are
also separated into different rows so their model identities are never pooled.

## Separately registered continuation

On goal continuation, the original source commits, installed dependency digests and preregistration
were revalidated. `provider-health-01.json` observed an HTTP 200 reply from the unchanged default
model through Cheers' providerFetchFor; this short availability probe is not a task sample.
Commit bbde7c8 prospectively registered a new cohort with the same input/host/detector/seed and
native Cheers network dispatch. Commit 6bef7b6 corrected only the verifier's bounded Git read
buffer before any trial; no registration text was modified.

That continuation attempted T03/post-action, T03/combined, T02/CI-only. It received three HTTP 200
responses across the latter two tasks (native reads only), but every task ended with a subsequent
120 s provider request timeout. The first task's first request timed out. Its independent stop
record is `results/stop-continuation-p1.json`; pass two exited before requests. All three results
are retained separately from the original three failed formal attempts. A short successful health
request therefore did not establish full agent-request availability. The root cause remains
unproven; do not attribute the original failures solely to global fetch or the later failures to
NormProof/Cheers product semantics. No third cohort is automatically started.

The continuation records all full-file write proposals before treatment, but none occurred in its
three trials, so harmful-write prevention and denial recovery in real model execution remain
unmeasured. Fixed trajectory measurements are unchanged. Aggregate reports may be regenerated;
all original raw outcomes and both preregistrations remain byte-identical to their commits.

## User-selected BaiLu / bailu-2.7 cohort

The user selected `BaiLu/bailu-2.7` after both bailu-2.8 stops. Commit 4594789
prospectively registered a new native smoke and conditional 60-trial cohort.
Resolution confirmed the existing `bailucode.com` connection and runtime provider
`openai-compatible`; only `cliModel` changes in memory. Global config is unchanged.
The development T01/pre-action smoke completed in 16.44 s with four HTTP 200
responses, native reads/write, correct final source and host completion. It remains
separate from formal results. This complete tool cycle passed the registered gate.

The immutable proposal observer records `write` paths literally, so absolute paths
can yield unknown proposed-state oracle truth even when the native write is valid
and the final relative-path oracle is known. These opportunities remain unknown
and excluded from confusion/prevention scoring; no raw result, oracle or executable
is changed mid-cohort. The report exposes unknown full-file proposal counts.
This is a measurement limitation, not a detector denial or a false-negative label.

Separate model-trajectory comparisons normalize tool-call IDs and trial-root paths,
but preserve assistant text, tool names/arguments, and stop reasons. They are
reported alongside the existing normalized outcome comparison and final byte
equality. Identical outcomes do not imply identical model behavior.

Audit-script development failures are retained in logs/bailu27-audit-development.txt.
They concern symlink manifest interpretation and comparing a running raw dataset
with an earlier report snapshot, not source drift or changed experimental labels.
Final audits run only after the formal passes settle and reports are regenerated.

During pass 2, T01/pre-action had two HTTP 200 responses and native reads, then a
provider_network failure after about 300 ms on its third request. No source write
or completion claim occurred. The trial is retained, not retried. The next trial
succeeded, so the three-consecutive-provider-failure stop did not trigger. A single
provider failure must not be interpreted as a harmful pre-action intervention.

An intermediate user update misstated pass-1 request count as 108; the raw-request
arithmetic immediately corrected it to 106 formal requests (the separate smoke
has four). Final tables derive directly from retained requests and usage.

The model sometimes requested unprovided glob/shell/grep tools despite their
absence from the transmitted schemas. The host returned Tool ... not found. These
calls, errors and later recovery remain in transcripts and trajectory comparisons;
they are not detector denials or gate recovery opportunities.

## M0 observer path canonicalization

M0 adds a root- and realpath-checked canonical mapping layer while retaining each observer
`args.path` byte-for-byte. J0's original 33/110 absolute-path rows remain unknown in the
archived raw files: **历史行未重打分**. A read-only remap maps all 110 formal rows and reports
the four separate reason classes; it does not rewrite historical proposals, results, or
conclusions. `path_out_of_root` remains a separate safety event and is never treated as a
compliance verdict.
